correctness.rationale: For an exact block p^a, phi(p^a)*sigma(p^a)=p^(2a)−p^(a−1), giving both the product identity and F(p^a)=p^(a−1). For n=m p^a q^b with distinct p<q and gcd(m,pq)=1, the remaining normalized product is in (0,1]. Thus F(n) is at least m² p^(a−1)q^(b−1)(p^(a+1)+q^(b+1)−1), which is at least 2²+3²−1=12. Equality forces m=1, a=b=1, and p=2,q=3, and F(6) really is 12. On n>1 the smaller fibers follow by enumerating p^(a−1)=1,2,...,11: 1 gives precisely the primes, 6 and 10 are not prime powers, and positive prime-power targets p^j give the single input p^(j+1). No power of one prime gives 12. The sub-12 equivalence is on n>1, as stated by the proof; F(1)=0 if one includes the unit. The supplied verifier was inspected but not executed; the symbolic bound proves exhaustiveness independently of the finite range.
residual_risks: No fibers above 12 are classified. The restriction n>1 is essential in the sub-12 equivalence.

value.rationale: This is the first possible defect for mixed prime support, not an arbitrary numerical cutoff. Up to the cutoff the exact defect determines whether the input is a prime power, and for 2≤F(n)≤12 it determines the entire fiber, including two gaps and the first mixed case. The contribution is modest but structural; listing the known prime-power evaluations alone would not suffice.
residual_risks: The bound establishes no general classification of larger fibers or monotonicity.
